newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, but most traders were sidelined due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives, dealers said on Friday.
Import and export prices and the Federal budget for February are due for release later tonight but will probably be non-events, they said.

"Rates were steady to higher in the morning on some position adjustments and weekend booksquaring. The market is just waiting for the (U.S.) Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25, for more clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend and Monday/Tuesday were unchanged from Thursday's common 5-1/4 5-1/8 percent, respectively.
Week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent.

Among longer dates, one month rose 1/16 point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, three-months rose 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16, nine-months rose 1/16 point to 6 5-7/8 and twelve-months rose 1/16 point to 6-3/16 6-1/16 percent.
